terra.problem: “He doesn't waste a second” adds a timing detail the text doesn't give.
The explanation repeatedly restates the answer and sounds generic rather than like Papa Dorin.
Saying healing is the only thing on the centurion's mind claims knowledge of his thoughts that the text doesn't give.
“Loud and proud” attributes pride and a volume of speech to the elders. The text says they pleaded earnestly.
The explanation repeats the answer and ends with generic instructional language rather than Papa Dorin's voice.
The explanation is flat and repetitive. “Close to the sound of it” also doesn't clearly connect to the answer.
“There's no hurry in it at all” rules out a sense of urgency that the text doesn't address.
“He's holding the door shut politely” adds an action the text doesn't describe.
Papa imagines himself as the person Jesus spoke about in the Bible event. He is never part of a Bible event.
Jesus tells the crowd about the centurion's great faith; the text doesn't say He tells them He is amazed.
